text.p: Sweden's powerful Wallenberg family is paving the way for an imminent merger between major banks S-E-Banken and Nordbanken by tightening its grip on S-E-Banken, analysts said on Friday.

Investor, the key holding company in the Wallenberg's financial empire, said on Thursday it had lifted its S-E-Banken stake to 5.83 percent of capital and 6.09 percent of votes from 2.49 and 2.61 percent respectively.
Including Investor's stake, the Wallenbergs now hold at least 17 percent of the bank that is seen as a Wallenberg bank.
"It is possible the Wallenbergs increased their S-E-Banken share holding to prepare for a merger (of the bank and rival Nordbanken)," Jonny Sylven, Swedbank analyst, told Reuters.
Investor has said it moved because the financial sector was "interesting". It could not be reached for further comment.
Analysts say the Wallenbergs are probably aiming for a merger with Nordbanken of which the state holds 59 percent.
Merger talks between the two collapsed in early February.
No reason for the breakdown was given but market players said it came down to differences over management with Nordbanken wanting both chief executive and chairman posts.
"Apart from S-E-Banken's management, all large parties -- the state, Investor and Nordbanken -- have said they regret that merger talks failed," Sylven said.
With two bank marriages already settled in Sweden's banking sector, the pressure is mounting for the only two large players not in merger talks to act.
Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced a merger on Tuesday this week and Handelsbanken on Monday finalised its acquisition of mortgage bank Stadshypotek.
"I wouldn't be surprised if they had serious discussions again," said analyst James Alexander of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
"They will have to climb down from both sides. But one side needs to get the upper hand to make sure the merger is seen through and to avoid in-fighting, which is a danger."
Several analysts expected a merger to happen fast.
"They should do it fairly quickly," Alexander said.
"They don't want to be left behind by the other two networks. To start now and finalise integration soon would mean a much stronger competitive advantage."
Sylven said he thought it would happen in the first quarter of 1997, if at all.
But analyst Goran Kallebo at Matteus brokerage expected a more long-drawn process.

"Merger talks might be taken up in half a year," Kallebo said. "It is a question about who will get the power. I think we will first see the Wallenbergs increasing in S-E-Banken and the state decreasing in Nordbanken."

Analysts expected a share deal, not a cash bid as neither bank could afford it. They doubted previous rumours that Investor would buy the state's Nordbanken stake as it is worth as much as 28 billion crowns ($3.8 billion).
Currently, Nordbanken has a total market capitalisation of about 49 billion crowns while S-E-Banken is somewhat smaller at around 42.5 billion crowns.
In late trade Friday S-E-Banken was 0.5 crowns higher at 81.50 crowns and Nordbanken was 11 down at 260 crowns.
-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 7.411 Swedish Crowns)
